justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Small positive effects for tendinopathy; not superior to other manual techniques when controlled.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: 1-2 day GTOM course; ~$500-800 plus tool purchase; moderately accessible.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable to soft tissue and musculoskeletal caseloads; usable in outpatient ortho and sports settings.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Billed under manual therapy codes; no Graston-specific billing premium over standard manual therapy.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Widely adopted technique; moderate employer demand in outpatient PT and sports medicine.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Novel technique can enhance perceived treatment intensity.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Patients will pay cash for hands-on soft-tissue work, especially in sports/ortho settings. Tool-based delivery feels tangible and 'premium' to consumers.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Supports modest upcharges but Graston is widely held and increasingly commoditized by competing IASTM brands (HawkGrips, RockBlades).
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Too common among ortho/sports PTs to be a true differentiator anymore; expected baseline rather than standout.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Protocol-based and trainable — other clinicians in a practice can deliver it, which is good for scaling beyond the owner.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Decent consumer recognition via athletes/social media, though most patients don't seek it by name.
justifications.business.efficiency: Short weekend course, relatively cheap, immediate clinic application — high ROI on time.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Commercial brand cert with minimal weight in faculty hiring or promotion files.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Some studies exist but quality is mixed and largely industry-adjacent; not a scholarship engine.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Can be mentioned in musculoskeletal modules but most DPT programs treat IASTM as one option among many.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Evidence is equivocal — small RCTs, modest effects, debated mechanism vs sham.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Rarely listed as preferred in academic job postings.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Cheap and quick, but the academic payoff is small so efficiency is moderate at best.
